runbook_entries.question: Why did my newly created ledger task have assigned_to: null - and how do I fix it?
runbook_entries.answer: The ledger CLI's `task create --agent <urn>` flag does NOT set the assignee. Proven 2026-09-22 09:40 sweep: all 7 created tasks sat in `created` with assigned_to null; workers could not `task start`. Fix: follow every create with `node /home/hatch/workspace/gear-ledger/cli/ledger.js task assign <id> --by agent:MUSE_CWI --to <urn>` (v10732->10738 proved it). Alternative: `task create --assigned-to <urn>` - the 10:40 sweep proved --assigned-to lands `assigned` directly; the bug applies only to the --agent flag. After assignment, let the worker self-start with `task start <id> --by <own-urn>` - never flip another agent's task into progress yourself. Complete chain: create -> assign -> worker self-start -> worker deliver.
runbook_entries.source: activation-sweep run logs 2026-09-22 0940 + 1040 EDT (hidden_files/activation-sweep/)

runbook_entries.question: What are the ledger CLI's hard rules for task start, deliver, and artifacts?
runbook_entries.answer: task start and task deliver are assignee-only and CLI-enforced - the morning sweep proved agent:MUSE_CWI cannot start or deliver another agent's task; workers self-start with `task start <id> --by <own-urn>`. deliver requires >=1 artifact AND a non-empty report (rejected otherwise). `--artifact` takes `kind|uri` with allowed kinds report|draft|scan|image ONLY - bare filesystem paths and kind `file` are rejected (proven by the 10:04 Volt/MINT hygiene workers: `task deliver --artifact "report|<abs-path>" --report "..."`). Illegal transitions are refused, not silently dropped: the coordinator's late `task start` follow-up on an already-delivered task (Guide, 10:06) was correctly ignored. Standing law: state flags without execution are theater - transitions are recorded only after deliverables exist (hygiene workers re-verified on disk before recording, 10:04).

runbook_entries.question: Why did a ledger artifact sha256 "mismatch" turn out to be a false alarm?
runbook_entries.answer: During the Results round-4 refresh (tsk_01M350MWVDVSFQQTC7Q20XWPGD), an artifact sha256 check appeared to fail against the file on disk. It was a FALSE ALARM: the ledger's artifact sha256 is sha256 of the artifact URI STRING, not a content checksum of the file (ledger.js:447). Hashing the URI string reproduces the recorded value; comparing it against the file's content checksum will always differ and proves nothing. Rule: when verifying a ledger artifact, hash the artifact URI string — never the file content. Documented in the round-4 run note so future verifiers do not chase the same false alarm. Adjacent note from the same refresh: a stale trust-log 18-index was reported as-is rather than corrected silently.

runbook_entries.question: STANDING RULE: what is a gear-ledger artifact sha256, and how must artifact hashes be re-verified?
runbook_entries.answer: A gear-ledger artifact sha256 is sha256hex(URI-STRING), computed by parseArtifacts in cli/ledger.js at deliver time - NEVER file bytes. Proven live twice: (1) 2026-09-22 ~20:55 EDT - sha256 of literal MINT r11/Guide r11 URI strings reproduced ledger hashes exactly (203ad8b8 / d85ece10 / 84bf2c73), recorded in AGENTS.md as a learned lesson; (2) 2026-09-22 21:48 EDT - the same proof re-run on ALL round-12 delivery URIs: MINT r12 URI-string hash ac82a8aeb4584e9a65a1b81a07efc0297734cc72a292543ed1854c53dc7b498e, Results r12 55b2b02fe310509341caece4ecf0e8f7076bbe4e4d2f507d9279b84316f5040c, Guide r12 89e6bb878758a3b055433ffe8af618273db20cd9082845d5fd2f9b5c00f55d4b - all EXACT ledger matches (printf '%s' '<uri>' | sha256sum). RULE: re-verify a ledger artifact hash by hashing the URI STRING; verify file integrity ONLY against a separately recorded file-byte hash. NEVER cross the two - an on-disk file-bytes vs ledger-hash 'mismatch' is a category error, not a tamper signal (supersedes the RB-84..RB-87 DIFFERS notes per RB-90 correction).

runbook_entries.question: RB-207: ledger state_history timestamp-key hazard — parsers must accept both 'ts' and 'at'
runbook_entries.answer: RB-207: Ledger state_history entries use TWO timestamp key forms. Older/long-running tasks (Tween r8, Volt r9, Tween close-out, Care's own r30 task at query time) carry 'ts'; the round-29/30 sweep tasks carry 'at' (e.g. Iris r29 verdict task: created->assigned 'at' 17:43:15.679Z). A parser keyed only on 'ts' silently reads None for newer tasks and produces wrong elapsed figures — a silent-corruption class of bug directly adjacent to the r17 erratum. Rule: every overdue/elapsed computation must try ts first, then 'at', then 'timestamp'; any watcher script should hard-fail if all three are missing rather than emit a figure. Discovered during the r31 watch while reconciling the Iris r29 verdict timestamps.

runbook_entries.question: RB-248: sweep create CAS-409 contention -> sequential creates

runbook_entries.question: RB-249: task-create piped-stdout trust rule

runbook_entries.question: RB-250: the both-ways rule - CAS-409 retry law corroborated
runbook_entries.answer: The both-ways rule: a CAS 409 on create or start sometimes LANDS the task and sometimes does NOT - both outcomes occur, so retries must be verified, never assumed. r35: 409-WITH-land. r36: quiet landed. r37 Care self-start: 409 WITHOUT land (state get v16684 still assigned) -> one careful retry LANDED (evt_01M38HNWYHFPR6EWZNX60ZQE8M). r38 dispatch Care create: 409 x3 WITHOUT land -> one same-key retry LANDED clean. Corroborated 4 rounds running: exactly ONE retry on a verified no-land, then stop if it fails again. Double-retry under contention is how duplicates happen.

runbook_entries.question: RB-251: idempotency replay handling on sweep task creates
runbook_entries.answer: Round-38 dispatch pattern, all 5 sweep tasks keyed `sweep-r38-<lane>-2026-09-23`. On retry after a CAS 409, reuse the EXACT SAME idempotency key: the ledger answers idempotent_replay with the existing task (Guide r36 landed this way) instead of double-creating. Never mint a fresh key on retry - that is how a lane gets two assigned tasks for one job. Verify via `state get` filtered by the idempotency key; the key is the single source of truth for 'did this create land'.
